newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Gucci sags on yen worries.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Gucci sags on yen worries.

text.p: Luxury goods company Gucci Group NV fell Thursday, hit by worries about a weak yen, traders and analysts said.
American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) in Gucci were off 4-1/2 to 69-7/8 in volume that put the company on the New York Stock Exchange's most-active list.

The company reported fiscal first quarter sales were up 31.5 percent. However, executives in a conference telephone call said sales in April had been weak in part because of a weaker yen that limited buying by Japanese.
Analysts who listened to the conference said the weakness could continue into May.
"People are reacting to the yen, and the yen's impact on Gucci sales," said Stacy Pak, an analyst for Credit Suisse First Boston in San Francisco.
However, she added, "I'm saying it's a buying opportunity and the reaction to the yen is overdone."
Among other ADRs, Irish airline Ryanair Holdings Plc soared in its Nasdaq debut. The shares were at 25-3/8 in mid-afternoon after pricing at 14-3/4.
Volume was 6.9 million ADRS, putting the company sixth on the Nasdaq's most-active list.
Irish drugs company Elan Corp also was up 1-1/8 to 40-3/4 in heavy volume.
Among Latin American ADRs, Argentine oil company YPF fell 3/4 to 29-1/4 in heavy trade after the company said it planned to list the 10 percent of its share capital it had awarded to employees.
Advancers edged decliners 261 to 255 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.07 percent and volume in mid-afternoon was 56.3 million shares.
ADRs allow U.S. trading of foreign shares.
